reviews.text: Despite my modest 21h in this game on steam, I spent almost 3 years being a part of the community with over 300 hours spent in test versions outside steam. Decks of Dexterity is a roguelike deckbuilder bullet hell game, it's a weird combination but it works. Made by a solo indie developer as his first ever fully fleshed out steam game. It definitely isn't perfect but I personally had my fun playing it and many people probably will too. [hr][/hr] [h2][b]TLDR:[/b][/h2] [list] [*]If you like [b]roguelikes[/b], you won't be disappointed. [*]If you enjoy [b]card games[/b] like Slay the Spire, you'll get a similar experience here. [*]If you're a [b]competitive[/b] player, almost every thing in this game can be speedrun and has its own leaderboard. [*]If you enjoy immersing yourself in the [b]story[/b], it's not for you. While it exists I wouldn't call it very advanced. [*]If you enjoy creating for the community, there is a [b]modding[/b] system with already a few existing mods (one even made by me) and a somewhat bad but manageable way to create your own cards. [*]If you're a fan of [b]bullet hell[/b] games and enjoy the dexterity part, you might not entirely get what you want. While dodging is a part of the gameplay, it's more focused on building a strong deck and taking damage is a huge part of the process, sometimes completely ignoring it being an option. [*]If you enjoy [b]hard[/b] games, you have such an option here with difficulty scaling like ascension in StS. [*]If you're a [b]casual[/b] player, beginnings will probably be a bit unforgiving, especially some of the campaigns. [*]If you enjoy big numbers and [b]high scores[/b] say no more, we have all that and some more, you can even enjoy single digit fps if you try hard enough, there's little limit. [*]If you prefer good [b]graphics[/b], you won't find them. Most of the game is made with basic shapes which for some might be neat but you won't find raytracing. [*]If you pay more attention to [b]music[/b], I won't comment much since I myself don't know much about music. It's quite basic, like a standard one person indie game. You won't find Silksong level music here. [/list] [hr][/hr] [h2][b]Positives[/b][/h2] + Highly replayable + Unique concept + Modding is supported + Very diverse card options + 4 main classes with completely different playstyles + Player feedback is taken into account + Gameplay is quick and smooth, pauses in time to play cards may seem disruptive for some but with some experience it feels good + Not very demanding game at baseline, you should get decent fps on most PC these days + An endless mode made for people who want to build broken decks [h2][b]Neutral[/b][/h2] [list] [*]Music exists, neither good or bad in my opinion but I prefer to play with my own [*]Story exists, it won't earn any prizes and is entirely skippable without any problems [*]Chaos, often there's so much things happening on your screen you have no idea what's going on [/list] [h2][b]Negatives[/b][/h2] - Some cards are clearly better than others with not much point in ever taking the useless ones - Some mechanics and enemies may be unfair and unforgiving - Game speed seems highly variable, sometimes in later stages being much too fast - Endless mode is a bit restrictive increasing difficulty without a way to turn it off [hr][/hr] [h2][b]Details[/b][/h2] This game puts most of its focus on cards, deckbuilding and creating broken combos. I'd say dodging is optional and story not that interesting. There's much inspiration taken from Slay the Spire and I myself found much replayability. I'd say after 50-100h you might find the deckbuilding part a little stale after finding out the best cards and combinations with all the other ones not really worth it. Fortunately I like the difficulty curve you're offered, somewhat hard at the beginning, really fun and quite easy in the middle and for people craving something harder you can do things that are very hard and barely possible. Even after doing mostly everything in this game, I still find fun in competing for high scores and creating mods to experience something new or bump up difficulty even higher. I'd say speedrunning and leaderboards are a huge part of the experience and are the part I found most replayability so far, there's an in-game leaderboard that gets refreshed monthly with new ways to compete each time. Creating mods is a bit clunky with very obscured documentation and weird custom "language" written in json files but if you had some experience with programming, it's easy to pick up. Main boss fights are highly unique and gameplay feels smooth. Tutorial is fine albeit some things are implied and left unsaid for people to find out through trial and error. Scanner is useless. As far as I know the game is going to still be supported for quite a while after release with frequent updates. Developer is a very sociable person active in discord, quick to listen to feedback and fix any bugs found. Overall I don't regret the time I spent playing this game and I loved being a part of the community in those past few years.

Such a good game. I've been helping develop the game by being a beta tester but I has been great watching it improve. It is a great gem. It is amazing that it has been released on steam finally! Can't see to see the community continues to grow!

Overall I quite enjoy this game. I played the demo quite a bit before the full release to steam. I only really have a few complaints about it: -Certain enemy mechanics can feel quite unfair -certain card feel much better than others to the point where it almost feels like there's no point in getting the worse cards other than those two though there isn't really any complaints i have about the game

While I don't have many hours on the steam version of this game I have so many on the Opera GX version. This game is a super big blast. I am a big fan of Rougelike games and this one is easily one of my favorites. I find the best aspects is that it executes synergies really well and is so satisfying when you have a great run. Overall I really think this game is worth the time and the money. Truly amazing.

I've been playing this game ever since I discovered it on the gx games, been a blast and always had been, played as a beta tester and a long time member of its discord, the dev is a super chill guy, I was absolutely proud of the progress and the fact that it's release just so happened to be after my birthday just made it better, (Shoutout to Codedgames who gave me a steam key to this as a bday present! THANK YOU SO MUCH MAN!!) that aside it's definitely fun to replay this game over and over, it's addicting in a way
Picture Slay the Spire meets Gungeon, all with a Superhot feel to it. Fun combos, intuitive mechanics, and big numbers that go bigger

I played the demo when it first went on gx games, and then the proper demo when that was released, and now this full release. I can easily say this is probably one of the most fun bullethell/deckbuilder games i've played, and i'd reccomend it to anyone who likes those genres.

I played the steam demo and bought it when it released. This is the first game i bought with money and for how cheap it is, its amazing. Characters have distinctive playstyles and the community is really active. I like how you can unexpectedly become a god and then instantly lose everything the next fight. Definetely would reccomend.

bought this game as a pre-order and even played the demo, i can tell u this game is amazing in every way even for how simple the idea is. community is also amazing and i cant wait to get home and play this game all day.
bought it on a whim and i've done nothing but play it for the past few days. really good

I ran into this game on GX games while it was still in the early stages, and have been awaiting its release for a while. It's a wonderful combination of dodging projectiles and building unfathomably broken runs, all in an intuitive and enjoyable way. I can't wait to see what else is added, keep up the good work Coded :)

This literally takes my 3 favorite game mechanics and blends them together amazingly. Deck building, bullet hell and rouge likes. This game feels like when in the movie ratatouille the rat mixed that cheese and strawberry (dang that looked bomb). I always feel compelled to explore every part of the map to mid max my build and its so satisfying 2 turn or even one turn clearing an enemy encounter. This game has come so far from the beta build i played back in 2020, i have so many fond memories playing this during covid and it honestly makes me emotional seeing how far this game has come while I wasn't looking.

Don't be fooled by my low playtime on this game (I play it a lot offline and played to hell and back during the beta). This game is amazing. One of the best roguelike deckbuilders I have ever played. Full of action, fully interactions with npcs and broken card combos. A fun experience every run and plenty of different starting decks to choose from. The multitude of different gamemodes is wonderful, adding yet another layer of depth to a game that has been in the oven for years now, and one that I can say is definetly worth the buy. While this game does technically have a story, its not a "story game" per se, so you can treat the story as flavour text to the amazing gameplay. The visuals are certainly a choice, especially when it comes to enemies being big blobs, but the artstyle is unique enough to (in my opinion) set it apart from othr games. The handdrawn encounters with npcs are beautifully illustrated and always amaze me. The game is tiny and runs like a cheetah on the open plains, smooth as can be (does that analogy work?). 10/10. Would recommend.

Originally found this game on GX Games before it even released, now playing it's official release and can confidently recommend this game to anybody looking for an incredibly fun roguelike with a good amount of content to play through!
Decks of Dexterity is such a fun and unique game that is very addictive. The idea the developers had for this game is so great and I really hope everyone enjoys it as much as I do

I was following this game as a beta tester, and was very interested in the development of the concept of a bullet hell card builder. This game integrates these mechanics in a fun, highly repayable, roguelike experience. Some aspects of the game can be hard but only if you pick those modifiers/gamemodes. This game is super fun, and anyone interested should totally give it a try.
It's not as hard as I thought at first. The videos on YouTube make it seem harder than it actually is. Great game, multiple playstyles

Really unique blend of deckbuilding, card game and bullet hell. It seems hectic but keeping track of everything is actually pretty doable once you get used to the different aspects of the game. The time mechanics for one of the characters was really really cool and wowed me when I first tried it (still getting my head wrapped round that character!). Definitely worth a pick up and a try just for how unique it is!
Have you ever been addicted to crack? well me neither but I think this would probably come close!

I played the beta and loved this game. Now I have it on steam and I still love this game. Decks of Dexterity is the perfect, strange blend of genres that seem like they should never be able to mix, and yet it mixes so well. I love how unique it feels compared to other deckbuilders, bullet hells and turn based games it is.

It's got everything you could want - Roguelike - Bullet hell - Deckbuilder mechanics - F~S rankings - Speedrun encouragement But instead of being the tropey kind of game you would expect from that it has a certain sauce to it that gives it its own identity and makes it not really play like I think you think it would

First Impressions: A Bullet Hell "Turn-Based" Roguelike Deckbuilder. Great variety for powerful builds. Engaging presentation. Visually very dense. Expansive accesbility options luckily included. Fun!
